:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}&=2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ x_{1}-x_{2} &=0 \\ 2x_{1}-2x_{2} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Choose one coefficient nonzero and solve the remaining coordinate equations by substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{2}&=1 \\ x_{1}-(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives a nontrivial solution. Verify it directly:

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}
$$

The coefficients are not all zero, so the set is **linearly dependent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

The statement “$x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{0}$ only if $x_{1}=x_{2}=0$.” is **false**. The statement “$2\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{0}$.” is **false**. The statement “The set $\{\mathbf{a}_{1}, \mathbf{a}_{2}\}$ is linearly dependent.” is **true**.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{2}&=1 \\ x_{1}+(1)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=-1 \\ (-1)-(1)+x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=2\end{aligned}

$$
-\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+2\mathbf{a}_{3}=-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}=\mathbf{0}

$$
\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_{3}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
:question/worked-solution:
A set is **linearly independent** when the equation $x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}+x_{3}\mathbf{a}_{3}=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_{1}=x_{2}=x_{3}=0$. A nontrivial solution proves **linear dependence**.

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\mathbf{a}_{1}+\mathbf{a}_{2}+\mathbf{a}_{3}&=-4\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

Test the proposed combination:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\mathbf{a}_{1}+2\mathbf{a}_{2}-2\mathbf{a}_{3}&=2\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}-2\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ &=\begin{bmatrix}-6 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\ne\mathbf{0}\end{aligned}
$$

The homogeneous vector equation gives the coordinate system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x_{2}+2x_{3} &=0 \\ 2x_{3} &=0 \\ x_{1}-2x_{2}-x_{3} &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Read a coordinate with just one remaining unknown at each step:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x_{3}&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{3}=0 \\ -x_{2}+2(0)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{2}=0 \\ x_{1}-2(0)-(0)&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_{1}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Every coefficient must be zero. Thus the homogeneous equation has only the trivial solution and the set is **linearly independent**.

A failed candidate alone does not prove independence; the homogeneous-equation argument settles the classification.

:question/problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
\mathbf{a}_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_2=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathbf{a}_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

For real $x_1,x_2,x_3$, form the equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$. Its augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Carry out these operations in the order shown: $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$; then $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1$; then $R_3\leftarrow R_3+R_2$. Use the resulting pivots and free variables to decide which statements are true.

Select all that apply. If none apply, leave all boxes unchecked.
:question/worked-solution:
Place the three vectors in the columns of the coefficient matrix. The homogeneous equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ corresponds to

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_1+x_2+2x_3 &=0 \\ x_1+2x_2 &=0 \\ 2x_1+x_2+6x_3 &=0\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Append the zero right-hand side and use the following row operations in order.

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_2\leftarrow R_2-R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3-2R_1$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Apply $R_3\leftarrow R_3+R_2$:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The pivot columns are $1,2$. The variable $x_3$ is free. Set $x_3=t$ and back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}x_3&=t \\ x_2-2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_2=2t \\ x_1+x_2+2x_3&=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_1=-4t\end{aligned}
$$

Hence

$$
(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(-4t,2t,t),\qquad t\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

For every $t\ne0$, the coefficients are not all zero. Therefore there are infinitely many nontrivial solutions, and the vectors are **linearly dependent**. A zero final row imposes no additional constraint.

The vectors $\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2,\mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent. This is false. The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has infinitely many solutions with coefficients not all zero. This is true. The equation $x_1\mathbf{a}_1+x_2\mathbf{a}_2+x_3\mathbf{a}_3=\mathbf{0}$ has only the solution $x_1=x_2=x_3=0$. This is false.
